I started using a smart lock on my front door about five or six years ago, and over that time I've tried quite a few models. For most users, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a solid choice — it supports Apple Home, has built-in Wi-Fi, and offers a very complete set of unlock methods. Whether you prefer your fingerprint or a simple PIN code, it's basically covered.

HomeKit Weekly is a column dedicated to smart home accessories, automation tips, and everything related to Apple's smart home framework.

Supports Apple Home, but no Home Key

ULTRALOQ is positioning the Bolt Fingerprint as its first smart lock to offer full integration with Apple Home, and it's precisely that integration that drew me in. Honestly, to this day I still miss Touch ID on the iPhone. You can lock or unlock through the Home app or Siri, and if you have a HomePod or Apple TV as a home hub at home, the experience is no different from other Apple Home accessories — you can add it to automation scenes, control it remotely, and it's fully compatible with all kinds of scenes and automation routines.

However, for me, there's one feature that has always been missing: Home Key. Being able to simply tap your iPhone or Apple Watch to open the door — that's what truly feels like an upgrade. Although that's the one feature that's absent, it's not exactly a deal-breaker.

I'd like ULTRALOQ to consider adding this feature in its next-generation model, because with Home Key, this lock could go from "good" to "nearly perfect." At the same time, the lock also supports Amazon Alexa, Google Home, SmartThings, and IFTTT — so no matter which smart home platform you prefer, or even if you plan to switch platforms in the future, it offers excellent flexibility. It uses 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi rather than Bluetooth, meaning you can do basic remote control through its app without needing an extra bridge.

Plenty of ways to unlock

The Bolt Fingerprint offers a wide range of unlocking methods. The fingerprint reader can store up to 50 fingerprints and 50 codes, you can unlock through the phone app, automatically unlock as you approach the door, or use voice control via Siri, Alexa, or Google Assistant. Two physical keys are also included, so you won't be completely locked out if the battery dies. For me, a smart lock without a physical key as backup is absolutely unacceptable.

You can also set up to 50 custom codes, and create one-time or time-limited codes for friends, visitors, or cleaners. If you have a rental property, this feature alone is already worth the price of admission.

There's also a "Lock Mode" that temporarily disables all electronic unlock methods, including codes and app unlocking, giving people who are away from home for an extended period an extra layer of peace of mind and security. Personally, I don't feel these features are essential for a smart lock, but having them doesn't hurt either.

Installation and adding to Apple Home

Over the past few years I've installed more smart locks than I can count, so by now I'm pretty experienced. As long as I have the right tools, I can usually get it done in about ten minutes. Assuming you're replacing an existing modern deadbolt, the installation process doesn't require any wiring or drilling holes in the wall. A single Phillips screwdriver is enough, and remember to replace the strike plate on the door frame at the same time.

Once you add the lock to your Apple Home setup and assign it to a room, you can control it through the Home app or incorporate it into automations and scenes — triggering multiple actions at once, like having the lights turn on the moment the front door unlocks.

ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint overall review

Overall, if you don't need Home Key support, the ULTRALOQ Bolt Fingerprint is a reliable choice. Fingerprint unlocking will likely become your everyday go-to method. The installation process is also very simple and straightforward. I'm currently using this lock on my office door, because there are lots of laptops around waiting to be shipped out, and I want that extra layer of security. The auto-unlock feature when approaching the door is genuinely very useful, and you can see at any time who's come by and who's left. The fingerprint unlock feels to me just like using Touch ID in the old days.

You can buy the Bolt Fingerprint directly from Amazon or the ULTRALOQ official website.
